id_and_class.theory_title: Lewis and MacGregor’s Phase of Energy Resonator Model
id_and_class.summary: Edwin Lewis and Ronald MacGregor propose that consciousness involves a two-way exchange of energy between the mental domain and the physical brain. They posit a novel ‘dispositional energy’ that rises from ordinary physical energy the way vapor rises from a warmed liquid, and suggest that coupled resonators, possibly at the interface of astrocytes and pyramidal neurons, carry this energy back and forth.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a New Phase of Energy

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a phase of energy: dispositional energy generated from neural energy, carrying information and able to act back on the brain.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: A ‘two-way street’: neural activity gives rise to mental states (P → M), and mental states influence neural activity (M → P), for example by directing attention or vetoing action. Lewis and MacGregor keep energy within the physical domain and picture consciousness as gating its flow.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Strong emergence (dispositional energy emerges from physical energy as a new phase with its own causal power, possibly partly exempt from deterministic laws)
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Neural and metabolic energy, a hypothesized dispositional energy, resonator elements, and the fields that couple them.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through evolutionary reasoning and neurophysiological modeling; the proposed substrate could in principle be probed in cellular biology.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Resonator elements tuned near a common frequency that phase-lock and share energy through a field. All elements turn neural energy into mental states; only some act back on the brain.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (perceptions, feelings); mental causation; agency and ‘free won’t’
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Resonance: separated resonators tuned to a common frequency phase-lock and share energy through a field, allowing dispositional energy to be stored and moved quickly across the brain.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Dispositional energy is generated and maintained by particular molecular processes. Resonators convert neural energy into mental states, make partially free selections among themselves, and some feed energy back to alter brain activity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Their favored hypothesis places resonators in the mitochondrial Krebs-cycle machinery of astrocytes at the astroglial–pyramidal interface of the neocortex; electromagnetic-field models are an alternative substrate.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness is causal: it gates or modulates the flow of energy between parts of the brain, which requires it to have some energy of its own. This causal power is what makes it visible to natural selection.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Resonators coupled through a shared field phase-lock and make collective selections, which links distributed mental activity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Dispositional energy is information-bearing and flows along the M → P side of the street to influence neural activity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: If consciousness arose by natural selection, it must be physically instantiated, have a phenotype, and confer an advantage, so awareness must be able to modulate physical activity.
core_claims_and_evidence: An evolved consciousness must be a causal agent, so mind and brain must interact in both directions.
Mental causation requires a novel, information-bearing dispositional energy.
Resonance provides a way to set energy aside and transfer it quickly across the brain.
Krebs-cycle activity in astrocytes is a candidate source of dispositional energy.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Theoretical (evolutionary argument and bioengineering modeling); speculative

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The model requires a form of energy unknown to physics, and it is unclear how such energy could act on the brain without conflicting with established conservation principles. Lewis and MacGregor present the model as part metaphor, part hypothesis.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Whether a new kind of energy beyond known physics can explain mind–brain interaction without violating science remains open, as does how P → M transformation produces felt experience.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: The view sits between materialism and dualism: it keeps energy physical but treats the mental side as a distinct phase with causal powers and partial freedom from determinism.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Consciousness depends on specific molecular resonators producing dispositional energy; whether artificial systems could generate it is not addressed.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Dispositional energy is generated and maintained by molecular processes in living brain tissue, so it should not outlast them.

virtual_immortality.rationale: If consciousness is a physical phase of energy in particular cells, a software copy would lack the substrate that produces it.
